title: kwave-power-law-attenuation-calibration: Reproducible numerical & analytical audit of k-Wave power-law attenuation near y=1
description:
kwave-power-law-attenuation-calibration provides a fully reproducible 1-D and 3-D numerical and analytical audit of power-law acoustic attenuation in k-Wave (MATLAB and CUDA), explaining near-y = 1 failures directly from the fractional-Laplacian state equation and testing built-in workarounds.

Key Audit Findings (v1.1.0 Interior-Source Benchmark)

  • Parameter Transfer (y = 2): Copying a linear literature coefficient (y = 1) directly into k-Wave's quadratic model (y = 2) biases attenuation at 0.5 MHz by −50.24%. Matching at f0 reduces error to −1.14% (R² = 0.999997, cp = 3103 m/s).
  • Exact Fractional-Laplacian Mechanism Near y = 1: Default dispersion follows Treeby & Cox's denominator 1 − (y+1)α0c0tan(πy/2)ωy−1. At y = 1.01, k-Wave delivers a −57.37% frequency-independent attenuation deficit (analytical: −57.58%) and a +54.8% superluminal phase-speed shift (cp = 4798 vs 3100 m/s), matching the +57% 3-D peak-pressure excess. At y = 0.98, attenuation rises by +190.45% (analytical: +201.51%) while phase speed drops to 1819 m/s.
  • Unconditional Hadamard Blow-Up at y = 0.99: Recording both p_max and p_min reveals that 1-D and 3-D fail identically: at y = 0.99, effective stiffness M(k0) = −0.3505 < 0 drives unconditional elliptic blow-up to −9.4×10301 Pa in 1-D and ~1030 Pa in 3-D across all tested timesteps (the earlier v1.0.0 report of 10−5 Pa 1-D collapse was an artifact of recording signed positive p_max alone).
  • Audit of fitPowerLawParams & no_dispersion: k-Wave's built-in fitPowerLawParams restores amplitude near y = 1 (−0.78% to −1.41%) but preserves +54.7% to +103.7% phase-speed distortion, and still diverges for ydesired = 0.99. Exact y = 1 with no_dispersion tracks the linear law across 0.2–1.0 MHz (−0.16% to −1.59%, cp ≈ 3103 m/s) in MATLAB, but is rejected/ignored by the tested CUDA v1.3 binary.

100% End-to-End Reproducibility

  • All 1-D datasets, figures, scaling/grid checks, and fitPowerLawParams audits are generated from committed MATLAB code (src/matlab/run_all_benchmarks.m) using standard interior-source placement (index 35, PML = 20, 180 μs).
  • All figures can be regenerated without MATLAB via python src/run_experiments.py --plot-only and python src/plot_near_y1_frequency_scan.py.

GitHub Repository: https://github.com/Yuewang04/kwave-power-law-attenuation-calibration
